issues.description: The problem statement is inconsistent about the signature of messageOnMilk(): the UML and interface declaration show a no-argument messageOnMilk() method, but later textual instructions require messageOnMilk(double milkVolume). The provided solution and template usage implement the no-arg signature. This discrepancy will confuse students about which method signature to implement (no-arg vs. taking a double) and what the expected return format is.
issues.suggestedFix: Decide on a single canonical signature and update all artifacts accordingly. Either: (A) Keep the no-argument signature as shown in the UML and solution — update the textual description (remove the double parameter and the volume formatting) so it instructs students to implement messageOnMilk() returning e.g. "Seal [name] is milked"; or (B) Adopt the double parameter everywhere — change the Milkable interface to messageOnMilk(double milkVolume), update all implementing classes and template method usages to accept and forward the volume, and update tests and examples to call the new signature. Option A is the smaller change and aligns with the current template/solution.

issues.description: The problem description instructs a Milkable method with signature messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and expects the returned string to include the milk volume, but both the template usage and the solution define/use messageOnMilk() with no parameter and implementations omit any volume. This mismatch between the specified method signature/semantics in the problem text and the actual API in template/solution will confuse students about which method to implement and how to call it.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and adjust the example return text accordingly, or (B) change the template and solution to declare Milkable.messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update all implementations and call sites (e.g., Main.java and sing logic) to accept and forward the milkVolume and include it in the returned string ("[Animal Type] [name] is milked (volume: [milkVolume]L)").
